title: Treasury coupon announcement (20Y new-issue + 10Y TIPS reopening sizes) — the first read off the 11-04 refunding table
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream. TWO rows announce that day: `20-Year BOND` with announcement Thursday, November 12, 2026, auction Wednesday, November 18, 2026, settlement Friday, November 20, 2026 — note the ABSENCE of Treasury's own trailing `R` reopening marker, which makes this a NEW ISSUE, consistent with the 20Y's Feb/May/Aug/Nov new-issue cadence visible in fiscaldata (2026-02-18, 2026-05-20 and 2026-08-19 all new issues at $16B) — and `10-Year TIPS R T` with the same announcement date, auction Thursday, November 19, 2026, settlement Monday, November 30, 2026, where the R marks a reopening and the T marks TIPS. The same parse independently shows the PDF now extends to February 2027, which is what makes this date newly available: the 2026-09-05 pull of the same document stopped in October. Filed estimate on two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The ~11:00 ET slot is Treasury's standing coupon-announcement convention and is NOT separately sourced. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-09-10 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08), and it earns a slot because it CORRECTS that ledger's own quarter-horizon call. On 2026-09-05 that doc concluded the coupon-announcement channel had a dated expiry at 2026-11-12 — 'the first announcement whose size no current Treasury primary publishes' — because sb0590's anticipated-auction-size table stops at Oct-26. That is wrong, and this entry is the receipt: the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding lands EIGHT DAYS BEFORE this announcement and publishes the Nov-26 / Dec-26 / Jan-27 table, exactly as sb0590 (2026-08-05) did for Aug/Sep/Oct. Checked for a gap and there is none anywhere in the cycle: sb0590 covers every coupon announcement through 2026-10-22, and 11-04 covers 11-12 onward. So the channel is CONTINUOUS by construction, and 2026-11-04 is where the grid can CHANGE, never where publication stops. That is the load-bearing distinction for every rates ledger in this calendar that reasons from 'supply is settled in writing'. What this event will publish, per the grid rather than per any current document: the 20Y NEW ISSUE, which has printed $16B for 13 consecutive new issues since 2023-08-23 (24 reopenings at $13B over the same run, 37 auctions, zero deviations), and the second reopening of 10Y TIPS CUSIP 91282CRE3, which sold as a $21B new issue on 2026-07-23 and whose reopenings run exactly $2B below their own CUSIP's new issue in 14 of 14 cases across 8 CUSIPs and 4 years. Neither number is published today; both become published on 2026-11-04. This entry is the dated home for forward test FT-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-09-10-2, registered 2026-09-08 and scoreable 2026-11-13, which predicts the 11-04 statement publishes a forward size table and that this announcement's 20Y cell matches it — a test of the publication MECHANISM, not of the number. Session context: it shares the week with the 11-18 20Y auction and the 11-19 TIPS auction it sizes, and follows the 11-10 and 11-12 refunding auctions. The same PDF parse also carries announce dates 2026-11-19, 2026-12-03, 2026-12-17, 2026-12-24, 2027-01-07, 2027-01-14 and 2027-01-21, deliberately NOT filed as a batch off one pulse — eight calendar entries at once would be noise rather than information, and they remain primary-sourced and available to a future sweep. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry, and the proposing event carries symbols: [] with no macro-keyed house playbook.
